question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $8,$ the additive inverse of $-30$ modulo $8$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $-30$ modulo $8$ is the integer $0\le x<8$ such that

$$
x+(-30)≡0\,(\text{mod}\,8).
$$

First, we note that $-30≡2\,(\text{mod}\,8):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}-30 & ≡(-4)\cdot 8+2 & \,(\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡(-4)\cdot 0+2 & \,(\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡2 & \,(\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$

Also, note that $-2+2≡0,$ so $x≡-2\,(\text{mod}\,8).$ To write this in the required form, we use the following sequence of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡-2 & \,(\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡0-2 & \,(\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡8-2 & \,(\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡6 & \,(\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $-30$ modulo $8$ is $6.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-30+6≡-24≡(-3)\cdot 8≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** In general, the additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
